engine_responsibilities.name: Load Evidence
engine_responsibilities.description: Accept BOQIntelligenceResult from Evidence Contract as input.
engine_responsibilities.rationale: Engine consumes evidence, does not produce it.
examples: analyze_boq() returns BOQIntelligenceResult → Engine accepts it
Engine reads evidence fields: row_classification, hierarchy, detected_level_skips

engine_responsibilities.name: Load Rules
engine_responsibilities.description: Load validation rules from Validation Rule Registry.
examples: Engine loads V-001 (Required Field Presence) from registry
Engine loads V-004 (Total Rows Consistency) from registry

engine_responsibilities.name: Evaluate Rules
engine_responsibilities.description: Execute validation rule logic against evidence.
examples: V-003: Check if row_classification values are non-negative
V-007: Calculate code_rows / total_rows ratio
V-014: Count detected_level_skips (or None if unavailable)

engine_responsibilities.name: Produce Findings
engine_responsibilities.description: Generate deterministic validation findings from rule evaluation.
examples: V-002 finding: [] (all expected keys present)
V-004 finding: 0 (sum matches total_rows)
V-007 finding: 0.67 (code column 67% complete)

engine_responsibilities.name: Handle Optional Evidence
engine_responsibilities.description: Gracefully handle None values for optional evidence fields.
engine_responsibilities.rationale: Hierarchy and detection evidence are optional (include_hierarchy, include_detection parameters).
examples: If hierarchy is None, V-010 reports: hierarchy_available = False
If detected_level_skips is None, V-014 reports: None

engine_responsibilities.name: Enforce Rule Lifecycle
engine_responsibilities.description: Only evaluate rules with status = VERIFIED or APPROVED.
examples: Skip rules with status = DEPRECATED
Skip rules with status = RETIRED

engine_responsibilities.name: Maintain Determinism
engine_responsibilities.description: Ensure same evidence + same rules = same findings.
engine_responsibilities.rationale: Validation must be repeatable and reproducible.
examples: Run engine twice on same evidence → identical findings
No random behavior, no timestamps in findings, no external state

engine_responsibilities.name: Preserve EQ-0011 Boundary
engine_responsibilities.description: Never produce assessments, recommendations, or professional judgments.
engine_responsibilities.rationale: Engine observes and detects. Consumers interpret and decide.
examples: Engine reports: '3 level skips detected' (NOT: 'level skips should be fixed')
Engine reports: '0.67 code completeness' (NOT: 'completeness is poor')

engine_responsibilities.name: Report Rule Provenance
engine_responsibilities.description: Include rule_id, rule_version, category in finding metadata.
engine_responsibilities.rationale: Consumers need to know which rule produced which finding.
examples: Finding metadata: {rule_id: 'V-007', rule_version: '1.0.0', category: 'Completeness'}

consumer_responsibilities.name: Interpret Findings
consumer_responsibilities.description: Apply application-specific meaning to validation findings.
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine produces findings. Consumers decide what findings mean.
examples: CheckMate: 0.67 code completeness → display yellow warning
Formatter: 0.67 code completeness → no formatting change needed
Reporting: 0.67 code completeness → include in summary table

consumer_responsibilities.name: Display Findings
consumer_responsibilities.description: Present validation findings to users in application-specific UI.
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine has no UI. Consumers own presentation.
examples: CheckMate: Display findings in validation report table
Reporting: Include findings in PDF export

consumer_responsibilities.name: Filter Rules
consumer_responsibilities.description: Select which rules to run based on application needs.
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Consumers decide which validations are relevant.
examples: CheckMate: Run all 18 implementable rules
Formatter: Run only completeness rules (V-007, V-008, V-009)
Reporting: Run only detection rules (V-013 through V-018)

consumer_responsibilities.name: Configure Thresholds
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine reports ratios. Consumers decide what ratios are acceptable.
examples: CheckMate: code_completeness < 0.5 → error, < 0.8 → warning, >= 0.8 → pass
Formatter: No thresholds needed (only uses finding values)

consumer_responsibilities.name: Make Decisions
consumer_responsibilities.description: Decide what actions to take based on findings.
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine provides findings. Consumers make decisions.
examples: CheckMate: Block export if critical findings detected
CheckMate: Show recommendations to user based on findings
Reporting: Include findings in automated report

consumer_responsibilities.name: Manage User Workflow
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine has no workflow. Consumers own UX.
examples: CheckMate: Run validation → Show results → Allow user to accept/reject
Formatter: Run validation → Auto-format based on findings

consumer_responsibilities.name: Store Validation History
consumer_responsibilities.description: Persist validation findings for audit/history (if needed).
consumer_responsibilities.rationale: Engine is stateless. Consumers own persistence.
examples: CheckMate: Save validation results to database
Reporting: Include validation timestamp in report metadata

consumer_responsibilities.name: Verify Contract Compliance
consumer_responsibilities.description: Ensure consumer correctly uses Evidence Contract and Validation Engine APIs.
examples: Run Consumer Compliance Suite (EQ-0013)
Verify Rule IDs exist in Engine
Verify Finding Types match expectations

contract_responsibilities.name: Produce evidence from BOQRow[] input
contract_responsibilities.description: Generate deterministic structural evidence from BOQRow[].
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Evidence Contract owns evidence production. Engine consumes evidence.
examples: analyze_boq(rows) → BOQIntelligenceResult
Evidence includes: row_classification, hierarchy, detected_level_skips, etc.

contract_responsibilities.name: Return BOQIntelligenceResult
contract_responsibilities.description: Return structured BOQIntelligenceResult as the public evidence surface.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract serves as sole integration surface for all consumers.
examples: BOQIntelligenceResult has: row_classification, boq_statistics, hierarchy, detection_summary

contract_responsibilities.name: Maintain structural invariants
contract_responsibilities.description: Enforce structural invariants documented in Contract.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract guarantees structural invariants. Engine relies on guarantees.
examples: SI-RC-04: row_classification always has 5 keys

contract_responsibilities.name: Maintain semantic invariants
contract_responsibilities.description: Enforce semantic invariants documented in Contract.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract guarantees semantic invariants. Engine relies on guarantees.
examples: SE-RC-01: Same worksheet produces same classifications

contract_responsibilities.name: Enforce column detection rules
contract_responsibilities.description: Apply column detection rules to identify BOQ columns.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract owns detection logic. Engine consumes detection results.
examples: Detect item_code, description, quantity, unit columns from worksheet headers

contract_responsibilities.name: Manage include_hierarchy option
contract_responsibilities.description: Control whether hierarchy analysis is performed.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract owns output scope. Engine receives optional hierarchy evidence.
examples: include_hierarchy=True → hierarchy field populated
include_hierarchy=False → hierarchy is None

contract_responsibilities.name: Manage include_detection option
contract_responsibilities.description: Control whether detection analysis is performed.
contract_responsibilities.rationale: Contract owns output scope. Engine receives optional detection evidence.
examples: include_detection=True → detected_level_skips populated
include_detection=False → detected_level_skips is None

registry_responsibilities.name: Govern Rules
registry_responsibilities.description: Manage rule lifecycle (Candidate → Approved → Implemented → Verified → Deprecated → Retired).
registry_responsibilities.rationale: Registry owns rule governance. Engine executes rules.
examples: Add new rule via Engineering Question + Spike
Deprecate rule when evidence field removed
Retire rule after deprecation period

registry_responsibilities.name: Maintain Provenance
registry_responsibilities.description: Document complete provenance for every rule (13 required fields).
registry_responsibilities.rationale: Registry ensures traceability. Engine relies on provenance.
examples: Rule ID, category, evidence_fields, boundary_class, eq_source, etc.

registry_responsibilities.name: Enforce Taxonomy
registry_responsibilities.description: Ensure rules conform to validated categories (Structural, Consistency, Completeness, Detection).
registry_responsibilities.rationale: Registry enforces taxonomy. Engine executes categorized rules.
examples: Reject rules with category = Assessment (crosses EQ-0011)
Reject rules with category = Financial (insufficient evidence)

forbidden_responsibilities.name: Assess BOQ Quality
examples: Judge whether BOQ is 'good' or 'bad'
Rate BOQ on quality scale

forbidden_responsibilities.name: Recommend Actions
examples: Suggest fixes for level skips
Advise user to change quantities

forbidden_responsibilities.name: Perform Professional Judgment
forbidden_responsibilities.rationale: Engineering provides findings. Humans make professional decisions.
examples: Determine project feasibility
Assess cost reasonableness

forbidden_responsibilities.name: Modify Evidence
forbidden_responsibilities.rationale: Evidence is immutable. Only Contract produces evidence.
examples: Change row_classification counts
Edit hierarchy structure

forbidden_responsibilities.name: Modify Rules
forbidden_responsibilities.rationale: Rules are governed by Registry. Engine and consumers are read-only.
examples: Change rule logic at runtime
Add rules without governance

options.include_metadata: bool (default: True) — Include rule provenance in findings
options.skip_deprecated: bool (default: True) — Skip rules with status=DEPRECATED

structure.finding_type: str — Type of finding (presence, count, ratio, etc.)

engine_state_policy.stateless: Engine maintains no state between invocations.
engine_state_policy.deterministic: Same evidence + same rules = same findings (always).
engine_state_policy.immutable: Engine does not modify evidence or rules.
engine_state_policy.isolated: Engine does not interact with external systems (no network, no database, no filesystem).
engine_state_policy.pure_function: Engine is a pure function: Findings = f(Evidence, Rules).

no_duplicate_responsibilities.check: Each responsibility has exactly one owner.

no_layer_overlap.check: Contract produces evidence. Engine evaluates rules. Consumers interpret findings.

no_responsibility_migration.check: Engine responsibilities remain in Engine. Consumer responsibilities remain in Consumer.

no_ontology_drift.check: Evidence Contract ontology unchanged. BOQ Intelligence unchanged.

no_hidden_coupling.check: Engine depends only on Contract (not BOQ Intelligence internals).

no_yagni_violations.check: Engine implements only what 18 rules require. No speculative features.

engine_is_consumer.check: Validation Engine is a consumer of Evidence Contract.
